prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

We present an x-ray spectromicroscopic investigation of single-crystalline magnetic FeMn/Co bilayers on Cu(001), using X-ray magnetic circular (XMCD) and linear (XMLD) dichroism at the Co and Fe L3 absorption edges in combination with photoelectron emission microscopy (PEEM). Using the magnetic coupling between the ferromagnetic Co layer and the antiferromagnetic FeMn layer we are able to produce magnetic domains with two different crystallographic orientations of the magnetic easy axis within the same sample at the same time. We find a huge difference in the XMLD contrast between the two types of magnetic domains, which we discuss in terms of intrinsic magneto-crystalline anisotropy of XMLD of the Co layer. We also demonstrate that due to the high sensitivity of the method, the small number of induced ferromagnetic Fe moments at the FeMn-Co interface is sufficient to obtain magnetic contrast from XMLD in a metallic system.

outputs.L1: We present an X-ray spectromicroscopic study of single-crystalline magnetic FeMn/Co bilayers on Cu(001), employing X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) and X-ray magnetic linear dichroism (XMLD) at the Co and Fe L₃ absorption edges in combination with photoelectron emission microscopy (PEEM). By exploiting the magnetic coupling between the ferromagnetic Co layer and the antiferromagnetic FeMn layer, we simultaneously produce magnetic domains with two distinct crystallographic orientations of the magnetic easy axis within the same sample. We observe a pronounced difference in XMLD contrast between the two types of magnetic domains, which we attribute to the intrinsic magnetocrystalline anisotropy of the Co-layer XMLD. We further demonstrate that, owing to the high sensitivity of this method, the small number of induced ferromagnetic Fe moments at the FeMn–Co interface is sufficient to generate XMLD magnetic contrast in a metallic system.
outputs.L2: We report an X-ray spectromicroscopy study of single-crystal FeMn/Co magnetic bilayers grown on Cu(001). Photoelectron emission microscopy (PEEM) was combined with X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) and X-ray magnetic linear dichroism (XMLD) measurements at the Co and Fe L₃ absorption edges. The interaction between the ferromagnetic Co film and the antiferromagnetic FeMn film enables the simultaneous formation, within one sample, of magnetic domains whose easy axes follow two distinct crystallographic directions. The XMLD signals differ dramatically between these domain types, an effect we attribute to the Co layer’s intrinsic magnetocrystalline anisotropy in XMLD. We further show that the technique is sensitive enough to detect XMLD magnetic contrast in a metallic material even when it originates from only a small population of induced ferromagnetic Fe moments at the FeMn–Co interface.
outputs.L3:
This study combines X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) and X-ray magnetic linear dichroism (XMLD) with photoemission electron microscopy (PEEM) to investigate single-crystalline magnetic FeMn/Co bilayers grown on Cu(001). Magnetic coupling between the ferromagnetic Co layer and the antiferromagnetic FeMn layer produces domains in which the magnetic easy axis adopts two distinct crystallographic orientations within the same sample.

The two domain types display markedly different XMLD contrasts. This difference is attributed to the intrinsic magnetocrystalline anisotropy of XMLD in the Co layer, demonstrating that the XMLD signal depends strongly on the orientation of the magnetization relative to the crystal lattice. Moreover, the high sensitivity of the approach enables the detection of XMLD magnetic contrast arising from the small number of ferromagnetically induced Fe moments located at the FeMn–Co interface. These results highlight the value of XMCD- and XMLD-PEEM for spatially resolved studies of magnetic coupling and interfacial magnetism in ferromagnetic–antiferromagnetic heterostructures.
outputs.L4:
Single-crystalline FeMn/Co bilayers grown on Cu(001) were investigated by x-ray photoemission electron microscopy (PEEM) using both x-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) and x-ray magnetic linear dichroism (XMLD). Combining these complementary magnetic contrasts made it possible to image the ferromagnetic domain structure of the Co film and to examine the antiferromagnetic order in FeMn with high spatial and element specificity. Exchange coupling across the ferromagnetic–antiferromagnetic interface produced domains whose magnetic easy axes had different crystallographic orientations within the same sample. This configuration allowed the influence of spin orientation and crystal symmetry on the dichroic response to be compared directly without changing the specimen or measurement geometry.

The Co domains exhibited pronounced differences in XMLD contrast depending on the orientation of their magnetization relative to the crystallographic axes and the polarization of the incident x rays. The magnitude of this contrast variation was too large to be explained solely by geometric effects and was therefore assigned to the intrinsic magnetocrystalline anisotropy of Co. The results demonstrate that XMLD in a ferromagnet can contain substantial information about the coupling between the magnetic moments and the crystal lattice, rather than reflecting only the angle between the x-ray polarization and the magnetization.

The element-selective sensitivity of the spectromicroscopy measurements also revealed a weak XMCD signal at the Fe absorption edge. This signal originated from a small number of Fe moments at the FeMn–Co interface that had acquired a ferromagnetic alignment through proximity and exchange coupling to Co. Detecting these interfacial moments illustrates the high sensitivity of the combined XMCD, XMLD, and PEEM approach. Overall, the study shows that this methodology can simultaneously resolve ferromagnetic domains, antiferromagnetic order, magnetocrystalline-anisotropy effects, and minute induced magnetic moments at buried ferromagnetic–antiferromagnetic interfaces.
outputs.L5:
### FeMn Studied by XMCD and XMLD

FeMn is a metallic antiferromagnet widely used in magnetic heterostructures, particularly as an exchange-bias layer in combination with a ferromagnet. Its magnetic structure is governed by the antiparallel arrangement of atomic moments, which produces little or no net magnetization in the bulk. Nevertheless, interfacial uncompensated spins and magnetic anisotropy in FeMn can strongly influence the behavior of an adjacent ferromagnetic layer.

X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) is an element-specific technique sensitive primarily to the net magnetic moment. In FeMn systems, XMCD measurements at the Fe and Mn absorption edges can therefore reveal uncompensated or field-induced magnetic moments. The technique is especially useful for examining interfaces, where proximity to a ferromagnet may induce a small net polarization in the antiferromagnetic FeMn layer. Through magneto-optical sum rules, XMCD can also provide quantitative information about spin and orbital magnetic moments.

X-ray magnetic linear dichroism (XMLD), by contrast, is sensitive to the orientation of the antiferromagnetic axis even when the total magnetization is zero. XMLD arises from differences in X-ray absorption for linearly polarized light oriented parallel or perpendicular to the magnetic axis. It is therefore well suited to probing the Néel-vector orientation, antiferromagnetic domains, and magnetic anisotropy of FeMn. However, XMLD may also contain contributions from crystal-field effects and structural anisotropy, which must be separated from the magnetic signal through suitable reference measurements or temperature-dependent experiments.

Used together, XMCD and XMLD provide complementary insight into FeMn: XMCD detects uncompensated magnetic moments, while XMLD probes the compensated antiferromagnetic order. Their combination is particularly valuable for understanding exchange bias, interfacial spin configurations, domain formation, and magnetic coupling in FeMn-based multilayers and spintronic devices.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an abstract for a research paper on XMCD/XMLD-PEEM imaging of magnetic domains in single-crystalline FeMn/Co bilayers grown on Cu(001).
counterfactuals.output: We investigate the magnetic domain structure of single-crystalline FeMn/Co bilayers epitaxially grown on Cu(001) using x-ray magnetic circular and linear dichroism photoemission electron microscopy (XMCD/XMLD-PEEM). Element-selective XMCD imaging resolves the ferromagnetic Co domains, while XMLD contrast provides sensitivity to the antiferromagnetic order in the FeMn layer. The combined measurements reveal a pronounced spatial correlation between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic domain patterns, demonstrating that interfacial exchange coupling governs domain formation across the bilayer. Changes in FeMn thickness and magnetic-field history modify the domain morphology and the degree of interlayer correlation, highlighting the roles of antiferromagnetic anisotropy, domain-wall formation, and uncompensated interfacial moments. These observations provide a microscopic picture of exchange coupling and domain imprinting in a model epitaxial antiferromagnet/ferromagnet system and clarify how antiferromagnetic order contributes to exchange bias in FeMn/Co heterostructures.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize a study investigating magnetocrystalline anisotropy in FeMn/Co bilayers using X-ray magnetic circular and linear dichroism at the Co and Fe L3 edges.
counterfactuals.output:
The study used element-specific X-ray magnetic dichroism to separate the magnetic behavior of the ferromagnetic Co layer from that of antiferromagnetic FeMn in epitaxial FeMn/Co bilayers. Co \(L_3\)-edge XMCD tracked the magnitude and direction of the Co magnetization, while angular-dependent XMLD—especially at the Fe \(L_3\) edge—probed the orientation and domain population of the FeMn antiferromagnetic order.

The measurements showed that the bilayer’s anisotropy is not determined by Co alone. Interfacial exchange couples the Co magnetization to the FeMn spin structure, causing FeMn domains to reorient or become preferentially populated when Co is magnetized along different crystallographic directions. The data were consistent with a strong, crystallographically defined FeMn magnetocrystalline anisotropy and a largely non-collinear, often spin-flop-like relationship between the Co magnetization and the FeMn Néel vector. Thus, exchange bias and coercivity in FeMn/Co arise from the competition among Co anisotropy, FeMn magnetocrystalline anisotropy, and interfacial exchange coupling, rather than simply from a layer of rigid uncompensated Fe moments.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise scientific abstract describing how magnetic coupling between ferromagnetic Co and antiferromagnetic FeMn creates domains with differently oriented easy axes and strongly differing XMLD contrast.
counterfactuals.output: Magnetic coupling across a ferromagnetic Co/antiferromagnetic FeMn interface produces a laterally inhomogeneous anisotropy landscape. Exchange interactions align the interfacial FeMn spin structure with the local Co magnetization, stabilizing domains whose magnetic easy axes adopt distinct orientations. Because X-ray magnetic linear dichroism (XMLD) depends on the angle between the X-ray polarization and the antiferromagnetic axis, these domains exhibit strongly different XMLD intensities despite having similar chemical composition and structural contrast. The resulting XMLD domain pattern directly maps variations in the FeMn spin-axis orientation induced by coupling to Co. These observations demonstrate that ferromagnet–antiferromagnet exchange coupling can imprint domain-dependent anisotropies in FeMn and provide a mechanism for controlling and imaging antiferromagnetic order in exchange-coupled heterostructures.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Produce a journal-style abstract about X-ray spectromicroscopy of FeMn/Co/Cu(001), emphasizing PEEM measurements, anisotropic Co XMLD, and detection of induced interfacial Fe moments.
counterfactuals.output: We report an element-resolved X-ray spectromicroscopy study of epitaxial FeMn/Co bilayers grown on Cu(001). X-ray photoemission electron microscopy (PEEM), combined with polarization-dependent absorption spectroscopy, provides spatially resolved magnetic contrast across the antiferromagnet/ferromagnet interface. At the Co \(L_{2,3}\) edges, pronounced X-ray magnetic linear dichroism (XMLD) is observed, with a strong dependence on the relative orientation of the electric-field vector and the Co magnetization. The anisotropic line shape and magnitude of the Co XMLD highlight the combined influence of magnetocrystalline symmetry and interfacial exchange coupling, enabling ferromagnetic domain configurations to be distinguished with high spatial resolution. Measurements at the Fe \(L_{2,3}\) edges reveal a weak but reproducible magnetic dichroism localized near the FeMn/Co interface, demonstrating the presence of induced or uncompensated Fe moments coupled to the Co layer. These interfacial Fe moments provide a direct microscopic signature of magnetic coupling across the nominally antiferromagnetic FeMn layer and are likely relevant to exchange-bias behavior. The results establish PEEM-based spectromicroscopy as a sensitive probe of element-specific spin order and interfacial magnetism in antiferromagnet/ferromagnet heterostructures.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe the key methods and findings of an experiment that uses XMCD and XMLD with photoelectron emission microscopy to study magnetic domains and interface magnetism in a metallic FeMn/Co bilayer.
counterfactuals.output:
The experiment used element-specific x-ray photoelectron emission microscopy (XPEEM) on a thin metallic FeMn/Co bilayer:

- **XMCD imaging:** Images were recorded at the Co, Fe, and Mn \(L_{2,3}\) edges with opposite circular polarizations. Their normalized difference gives the projection of the ferromagnetic or uncompensated moment along the x-ray beam. Co XMCD therefore mapped the Co ferromagnetic domains, while weak Fe/Mn XMCD revealed net moments in FeMn, mainly associated with the interface.
- **XMLD imaging:** Images taken with different linear polarizations at the Fe or Mn absorption edges provided contrast proportional to the orientation of the antiferromagnetic axis. XMLD is insensitive to reversal of all spins, so it maps Néel-vector domains rather than the sign of the magnetization.
- **PEEM:** The emitted-electron images supplied submicrometre spatial resolution. The FeMn layer was kept thin enough that interface-related and Co signals remained detectable. Energy-dependent spectra and asymmetry images were used to separate genuine magnetic contrast from topographic or chemical contrast.

The main observations were:

1. **Co formed conventional ferromagnetic domains**, clearly visible by Co XMCD.
2. **FeMn retained antiferromagnetic order**, producing XMLD domains and domain walls that were not simply a one-to-one copy of the Co pattern, although their arrangement could be influenced by exchange coupling to Co.
3. **A finite Fe/Mn XMCD signal showed uncompensated or canted FeMn moments at the interface.** These moments were correlated with the local Co magnetization; Fe and Mn contributions could have opposite signs because of their antiferromagnetic coupling.
4. Thus the FeMn layer simultaneously exhibited a largely compensated antiferromagnetic domain structure and a much smaller interfacial net moment coupled to the ferromagnet.

The key significance was that combining XMLD and XMCD in the same microscope separated the two ingredients of exchange coupling: the antiferromagnetic Néel-domain structure in FeMn and the uncompensated interfacial spins that couple directly to Co and are relevant to exchange bias.
